AgentsKit Harness is the configurable, open-source SDLC loop for issue-to-release work. Public product documentation lives on the Fumadocs site at https://harness.agentskit.io/docs.

## Knowledge

- [artifacts](apps/docs/content/docs/concepts/artifacts.mdx): A worker's session is opaque: the harness cannot see its model calls, its tool calls or its reasoning. What it *can* see is a worktree. So the contract between the two is three files, at `.ak-loop/` in the worktree root.
- [connectors](apps/docs/content/docs/concepts/connectors.mdx): The stages talk to the outside world through three interfaces, chosen by `connectors.*`:
- [contracts](apps/docs/content/docs/concepts/contracts.mdx): A contract is the orchestrator's answer to one question: *what would make this issue done, and how would anyone know?* It is produced once, before dispatch, and frozen — the worker, the review and the merge gate all judge against the same text.
- [cost](apps/docs/content/docs/concepts/cost.mdx): Start with the limit: **the loop cannot count what a worker's CLI spends.** That session is opaque; its model and tool calls never reach the harness. Everything here is about what the harness itself decides — who it calls, how often, with how much context — plus circuit breakers on signals it can actually observe.
- [definition-of-done](apps/docs/content/docs/concepts/definition-of-done.mdx): "Done" in an unattended loop has to be decided without a human in the room. One checklist cannot do it: some things are true of every issue in a repository, and some are true only of this one. So there are two lists, and a merge waits for both.
- [events](apps/docs/content/docs/concepts/events.mdx): Every transition writes a line to `<stateDir>/events.ndjson` and emits on the plugin bus. Those events are how `debrief`, `observe`, `retro` and every notification channel know anything: the log is the source of truth, and no report keeps its own state.
- [flows](apps/docs/content/docs/concepts/flows.mdx): An incident and a refactor of the billing core should not cost the same. A flow profile is how one loop serves both without becoming two loops.
- [human-gates](apps/docs/content/docs/concepts/human-gates.mdx): The loop runs unattended. It stops in exactly these places, and the rule behind all of them is the same: **a human decides where the machine would be acting on the world, or acting on itself.**
- [layers](apps/docs/content/docs/concepts/layers.mdx): A layer is a slice of the repository with three things attached: the tracker label that places an issue in it, the globs it owns, and the one test that closes it.
- [memory](apps/docs/content/docs/concepts/memory.mdx): Memory here is not a vector database and not a chat history. It is a small set of **approved project decisions** that a human (or, within declared bounds, the retro) promoted, recalled into a prompt when they are relevant, and attributed so they can be revoked.
- [plans-and-votes](apps/docs/content/docs/concepts/plans-and-votes.mdx): With `worker.plan.enabled`, no worker is launched until a plan has consensus. The planner and the voters run **in the harness, headless, before dispatch** — the same shape as freezing a contract. The model writes the plan and writes the votes; the machine counts them and decides.
- [self-improvement](apps/docs/content/docs/concepts/self-improvement.mdx): A loop that runs for weeks accumulates evidence about itself. Doing nothing with it wastes it; acting freely on it is how an autonomous system drifts from what its owners agreed to, one defensible step at a time. So the loop may change exactly three things.
- [stages](apps/docs/content/docs/concepts/stages.mdx): A stage is a state machine the harness runs. A model may produce content — a contract, a plan, a vote, a review, an alert triage — but the machine reads that content and decides the transition. That is what makes a run reproducible: the same state produces the same decision, and the event log says which path it took.
- [state-machines](apps/docs/content/docs/concepts/state-machines.mdx): Every stage is a machine. A model may write the content a transition reads; the machine reads it and decides. These are the eight.
- [~/.agentskit/harness.yaml — yours, on this machine](apps/docs/content/docs/configuration/layers.mdx): One person runs the loop on several repositories; one repository is run by several people, on machines that differ. Four files, merged in order and validated **once, as one config**:
- [models](apps/docs/content/docs/configuration/models.mdx): Four roles pick from their own list: `orchestrator`, `reviewer`, `builder`, `watcher`. Each list is tiers, best first, and every tier is a set of `provider/model` references.
- [presets](apps/docs/content/docs/configuration/presets.mdx): `loop init` writes `loop.config.yaml` from a preset, and a preset is a set of **defaults**, not a template to fill in. Everything the preset already says is left out of the file it writes, so the config diff a reviewer reads shows what *this* project decided differently — and nothing else.
- [scheduling](apps/docs/content/docs/configuration/scheduling.mdx)
- [first-loop](apps/docs/content/docs/examples/first-loop.mdx): Ten minutes, four commands, nothing irreversible until the last one.
- [one-issue-three-flows](apps/docs/content/docs/examples/one-issue-three-flows.mdx): One motor, three kinds of demand. The issue is the same in all three: *the `/usage` endpoint returns stale counters after a plan change.*
- [plugging-in](apps/docs/content/docs/examples/plugging-in.mdx): Three ways to wire the loop into a setup it did not come with. None of them needs a fork.
- [the-day-it-escalated](apps/docs/content/docs/examples/the-day-it-escalated.mdx): An unattended loop is judged by how it stops. These are the four ways, in the order they happen to a real project.
- [first-issue](apps/docs/content/docs/get-started/first-issue.mdx): The first issue decides what you learn. Pick one that is small, provable and boring — the loop's failure modes are much easier to see when the work itself is not interesting.
- [how-it-works](apps/docs/content/docs/get-started/how-it-works.mdx): <LoopFactory />
- [installation](apps/docs/content/docs/get-started/installation.mdx)
- [quickstart](apps/docs/content/docs/get-started/quickstart.mdx): Four commands, in order. Each one is safe to run again, and nothing before the last touches your repository, your tracker or your schedule.
- [agents.registry.yaml](apps/docs/content/docs/guides/agents.mdx): A role can run on a provider alone, or on an agent the project installed — a directory of code and instructions that `npx agentskit add <id>` copies into the repository.
- [→ { "planId": "…", "question": { "id": "q1", "text": "…" } }](apps/docs/content/docs/guides/driving-plan.mdx): `loop plan` is built to be driven by an agent talking to a person. The machine asks one question at a time and decides when the interview is over; the person answers.
- [intake-and-maintain](apps/docs/content/docs/guides/intake-and-maintain.mdx): These two stages are what close the cycle: without them the loop only drains a queue somebody else fills.
- [local-runner](apps/docs/content/docs/guides/local-runner.mdx)
- [Loop observability — my-project · <person>](apps/docs/content/docs/guides/operating.mdx): Everything here is read-only. None of it dispatches, reviews, merges or writes to a tracker.
- [plugins](apps/docs/content/docs/guides/plugins.mdx)
- [release](apps/docs/content/docs/guides/release.mdx): `project.baseBranch` is where work integrates. `release.branch` is what reaches production. The release stage moves one to the other, and only for a batch someone approved.
- [troubleshooting](apps/docs/content/docs/guides/troubleshooting.mdx)
- [index](apps/docs/content/docs/index.mdx): `@agentskit/harness` runs one project's software development lifecycle unattended: a vague objective becomes a PRD, the PRD becomes a design and issues, each issue becomes a contract, a worker in its own worktree, a reviewed pull request proven against a definition of done, a merge — and, behind a human gate, a release.
